lesson.title: Two bars side by side
lesson.subtitle: P3 bridge and P4 bar-chart revision
lesson.objective: Read the second series of a double bar chart, find a difference and spot the biggest gap.
lesson.story: The double bar chart compares Boys and Girls for P4A, P4B, P4C and P4D. The key at the top shows which bar belongs to which group.

steps.title: Read the second bar
steps.prompt: Look at the Girls bar for P4D. What value does it show?
hints: Check the key at the top to see which pattern stands for Girls.
Find the pair of bars for P4D and choose the striped one.
The top of the striped P4D bar is level with the gridline for 10.

steps.title: Find the difference
steps.prompt: How many more are in the taller bar than in the shorter bar for P4D?
hints: To find how many more, take the smaller number away from the larger one.
Read both bars for P4D: Boys is the solid bar and Girls is the striped bar.

steps.title: Find the biggest gap
steps.prompt: For which label are the two bars furthest apart in height?
hints: A gap is how far apart the two bars of one pair are.
Look at each pair in turn and find the pair whose tops are furthest apart.
The gaps are: P4A 20, P4B 5, P4C 5, P4D 25.
P4D has the biggest gap. Choose P4D.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How does the striped pattern help you read a double bar chart?

choices.label: The striped bar is always the taller bar in each pair of bars.
The stripes show how many each bar stands for, like a scale.
The pattern and the key show you which bar belongs to which group.

hints: Think about the key at the top of the chart.
Each pair has one solid bar and one striped bar.
The key matches a pattern to a group.
Choose the explanation about matching bars to groups.
